prompt: What does the line `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` change on a phone?

choices.text: The layout uses the phone's own width
choices.why: Right. Without it the deals page was laid out 980 wide under the iPhone descriptor.

choices.text: It makes the server send the phone version
choices.why: The tag is read by the browser after the page arrives; the server chose the page already.

choices.text: It sets the device pixel ratio to 1 for every page
choices.why: The ratio belongs to the screen; under the iPhone descriptor it stayed 3 on every page.

choices.text: Nothing on a phone; it only matters on desktops
choices.why: The other way round: a desktop browser ignores it, and a phone obeys it.

prompt: A window 390 wide and the iPhone 13 descriptor both report a screen of 390. Which difference did `viewport.mjs` measure on the shop's main page?

choices.text: None: both reported the same innerWidth
choices.why: The phone reported 400, the desktop window 390.

choices.text: The phone's window measured 400
choices.why: Right. A phone honouring the viewport tag widens its window to fit a page that is 400 wide.

choices.text: The desktop window had a device pixel ratio of 3
choices.why: It was 1; the ratio of 3 came with the descriptor.

choices.text: The phone could not load the page without WebKit
choices.why: It loaded in Chromium; the script drops `defaultBrowserType` on purpose.

prompt: An iPhone 13 is 390 CSS pixels wide with a device pixel ratio of 3. How many device pixels wide is its screen?
`style.css` has `@media (max-width: 600px)`. Which pair of widths tests the line itself?

choices.why: Those test two layouts far from the line; a mistake at the line passes both.
Both are inside `max-width: 600px`, so both get the phone layout.
Right. 600 is the last phone width and 601 the first desktop one.
Both are outside the rule, so both get the desktop layout.

prompt: A test at 1280 px asserts `await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Menu' })).toBeHidden()`. Somebody renames the button *Navigation*. What happens?

choices.text: It fails, because the name no longer matches
choices.why: A locator that matches nothing counts as hidden, so the assertion holds.

choices.text: It still passes, proving nothing
choices.why: Right. That is why the lesson's file adds `includeHidden: true` and `toHaveCount(1)`.

choices.text: It times out waiting for the Menu button to appear on the page
choices.why: `toBeHidden` waits for hidden, and nothing matching is hidden at once.

choices.text: Playwright reports a strict mode violation
choices.why: Strict mode complains about two matches, not about none.

prompt: Which question is `page.setViewportSize` the right tool for, where `test.use({ viewport })` is not?

choices.text: What a phone's touch screen does to the page
choices.why: Both change only the window; touch comes with `hasTouch`.

choices.text: What this width gets when the page opens
choices.why: Either answers that; `test.use` is the plain way to.

choices.text: What a page does when the window changes while it is open
choices.why: Right. It resizes a page already open, in the middle of a test.

choices.text: Which page the server sends
choices.why: The width never reaches the server; neither option changes what it sends.

prompt: Under the iPhone 13 descriptor, why would `expect(scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(innerWidth)` pass on the shop?

choices.text: Because the iPhone layout hides the basket
choices.why: The basket line shows at every width; the Menu button hides the links, not the basket.

choices.text: innerWidth grew to 400, the page's own width
choices.why: Right. The phone widened its window to fit, so the page is compared with itself. Compare with the width you asked for.

choices.text: Because scrollWidth is in device pixels
choices.why: Both are CSS pixels; the ratio of 3 does not enter.

choices.text: It would not; it fails at 400 against 390
choices.why: That is the comparison with the width asked for; innerWidth reported 400 too.

prompt: The overflow test fails at 360 and 390 and the defect is reported, not fixed. Why does the lesson choose `test.fail` over `expect(scrollWidth).toBe(400)`?

choices.text: Because `toBe(400)` would fail on the day of the fix, reported as a regression
choices.why: True of `toBe(400)`, and only half the reason: it also calls the defect correct.

choices.text: It keeps measuring, and turns red the day the defect is fixed
choices.why: Right. 'Expected to fail, but passed' is the signal to take the mark off.

choices.text: Because `test.fail` skips the test, which is quicker
choices.why: It runs the test in full; skipping is the first of the three choices.

choices.text: Because a known defect must not appear in the report
choices.why: The list still draws the two failures with a cross on every run.

prompt: The full width of the page, which the overflow test compares with the window, is `document.documentElement.___` .
A desktop Chromium in a window 390 wide asks for `/deals`. Which page does it get?

choices.text: The phone page, because the window is phone-sized
choices.why: The server never sees the width; it reads the `User-Agent`.

choices.text: The desktop page, as at 1280
choices.why: Right. Its `User-Agent` has no `Mobile` in it, whatever the window.

choices.text: Whichever page a cache kept last
choices.why: `Vary: User-Agent` tells caches to keep the two apart.

choices.text: A 404, since `/deals` needs a phone
choices.why: Both kinds of browser get a page; `curl` got the desktop one.

prompt: `test.use(devices['iPhone 13'])` inside a `describe` block stops the run before any test. Why?

choices.text: It asks for WebKit, set per worker
choices.why: Right. Playwright refuses `defaultBrowserType` in a block; the lesson leaves it out.

choices.text: WebKit is not installed on this machine
choices.why: The error comes before any browser starts, and names `defaultBrowserType`.

choices.text: Device descriptors only work in `viewport.mjs`
choices.why: The fixed test file uses the same descriptor, minus one option.

choices.text: The iPhone's viewport is too small for the shop
choices.why: Size has nothing to do with it; the message is about the browser type.

prompt: A server answers phones and desktops with different HTML at one address but sends no `Vary: User-Agent`. What can go wrong?

choices.text: Phones fall back to a layout 980 pixels wide
choices.why: That is a missing viewport tag, a different defect.

choices.text: Browsers refuse to show the page
choices.why: Browsers show it; the trouble is in what a cache does between them.

choices.text: A cache serves one device the other's page
choices.why: Right. The defect then comes and goes with whoever asked first.

choices.text: The `User-Agent` stops being sent
choices.why: Browsers send it with every request whatever the server answers.

prompt: Everything in `tests/deals.spec.js` passes. Which claim does that support?

choices.text: The deals page works in Safari on an iPhone
choices.why: It ran in Chromium wearing an iPhone's name; WebKit was not run.

choices.text: A request with the iPhone's `User-Agent` gets the phone page
choices.why: Right. That is what the server decides from, and what the test controlled.

choices.text: Every tablet gets the phone page as well
choices.why: Twelve of Playwright's entries are tablets without `Mobile`, and they get the desktop page.

choices.text: The page is fast enough on a phone's network
choices.why: Emulation copies no processor and no network.

prompt: Match each check to the kind of page it belongs to, or to both.

pairs.left: A narrow desktop window gets the desktop page

prompt: `tests/targets.spec.js` lists *Shop* and *Search* as judged. How was that list made?

choices.text: The robot applied all of 2.5.8, and the person typed in its result
choices.why: The robot only measured size; the spacing alternative needs judgement.

choices.text: The test measured boxes; somebody looked at the spacing
choices.why: Right. A new small target fails until somebody looks at it too.

choices.text: The robot fixed the links' size
choices.why: A test measures; it changes nothing in the page.

choices.text: Nothing: the links are above 24 pixels
choices.why: They are under 24, which is why they are listed.

prompt: Turned on its side, the iPhone 13 descriptor is 750 wide. What does that mean for the shop?

choices.text: It keeps the phone layout, because it is still a phone
choices.why: The stylesheet asks only about width, and 750 is past 600.

choices.text: The server sends it the desktop deals page
choices.why: Its `User-Agent` still says `Mobile`; orientation does not change the name.

choices.text: It gets the desktop layout, in a window 342 high
choices.why: Right. It crosses the breakpoint, and whether that layout fits is worth a test.

choices.text: Nothing changes, since orientation is not emulated
choices.why: Playwright has a landscape entry with its own viewport.

prompt: Put a responsive check of a new page in order.
items: Read the breakpoints off its stylesheet
Pick the widths either side of each one
Assert what shows and hides at each width
Check that nothing scrolls sideways at each width
trap: The widths come from the stylesheet, so reading it comes first.

prompt: A site serves an adaptive phone page. Your tests emulate an iPhone and pass. What should you still check?

choices.text: Nothing; an adaptive page needs no responsive checks
choices.why: Each page the server can send is a page with a layout of its own.

choices.text: Only the desktop page, at 1280
choices.why: The phone page needs checks too: the deals one is laid out at 980.

choices.text: The phone page's own viewport tag and overflow
choices.why: Right. The deals phone page has no viewport tag, so a phone lays it out 980 wide.

choices.text: The phone page in a desktop window at 390 px
choices.why: A desktop window would be given the desktop page instead.

prompt: Which of these can a robot check with one right answer? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The page is no wider than a 360 px window
choices.why: Right. Two numbers, compared.

choices.text: The phone layout is pleasant to use
choices.why: That is judgement; a person looks, on a real phone.

choices.text: The phone request gets `Vary: User-Agent`
choices.why: Right. A header has one value.

choices.text: The Menu button sits where a thumb expects it
choices.why: Where a thumb expects it is a person's call.
